key_concepts: The respiratory system takes in oxygen and expels carbon dioxide
Air moves through the nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi, bronchioles, and alveoli
The epiglottis prevents food from entering the airway
The trachea is kept open by rings of cartilage
Alveoli are the main sites of gas exchange in the lungs
The diaphragm and rib muscles change chest cavity volume during breathing
Inhalation occurs when the diaphragm contracts and air pressure in the lungs decreases
The circulatory system transports oxygen, nutrients, and wastes throughout the body
The heart pumps blood through blood vessels
Arteries carry oxygenated blood away from the heart while veins return deoxygenated blood
Capillaries are the smallest blood vessels and are where gases and nutrients are exchanged
Pulmonary, coronary, and systemic circulation move blood through different pathways
